column6: The developer experienced a setback in August 2024 when a federal judge ordered an injunction against exploratory drilling while the judge rules on the merits of a lawsuit by the Hualapai Tribe and the nonprofit environmental law organization Earthjustice. The lawsuit challenged BLM's approval of the exploratory drilling, arguing that the project threatens Ha'Kamwe', a medicinal spring recognized as a traditional cultural property. The tribes also argued that BLM failed to consider reasonable, lower-risk options such as approving only 1 or 2 of 3 proposed drill sites, requiring the sites to be located further from sensitive areas, and requiring stricter controls on noise, light, traffic and vibrations. The tribes were also concerned that exploratory drilling might affect aquifers including wildlife, flora, fauna, and gathering areas.

column12: The Black Hills mining region of South Dakota is perhaps best known for its rich gold deposits like Homestake, where 44Moz was mined over 100 years. But, until recently, most people wouldn’t have been aware of its history as one of the largest producing lithium districts in the world from the late 1800s to the mid to late 1900s. It is not one of those lithium districts previously mined for its tin or tantalum – this was a true lithium mining district. That means the geology and metallurgy is well understood.  It also boasts the largest spodumene crystals (~6% lithium) in the world. How big? The Etta mine — at times the main source of spodumene in the world — yielded the largest (up to 15m long, weighing 90 tonnes) spodumene crystals ever mined.
